thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — after merging the new quantization recommendations (PR #423) I ran the staged eval suite. Latency improved (~18%) but summarization quality fell on the benchmark prompt set (score 0.92 -> 0.85). Putting this here for async triage and owner clarification. :warning:

sam: Yikes. Can you link the eval dashboard + the exact commit?

maria: dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/evals/summary/2123 commit: 1f4b9a3 (merged by @ravi). The failing set is `summarize-news-50` — diffs attached in the eval UI.

ravi: seeing it, thanks for flagging. I pushed the int8 kernel profile that reduced token compute, but maybe the precision tradeoff is worse for some prompts.

lin: tagging batching/caching owners — this might be interacting with cache TTL, we saw different prefix reuse in staging. @kai can you check cache hit distributions?

kai: looking now — cache hit rate dropped ~7% for that workload after the change. Could be because KV key hashing changed with the new quant kernels.

maria: FWIW the regression is concentrated on long-context prompts (700-1200 tokens). Short prompts unaffected.

sam: Ok, actionable list please: 1) rollback flag? 2) narrow canary? 3) root cause triage owners.

ravi: my proposal: flip the new quant flag to `canary` 10% for hosted, keep staging at 100% until we validate fixes. I can open a rollback PR if we want immediate revert.

lin: also suggest enabling `prefix-cache-compat` toggle in canary to isolate cache behavior. Config looks like: 

```
# rollout config snippet
rollout:
  quant_profile: int8_v2
  canary_pct: 10
  prefix_cache_compat: true
```

maria: +1 to canary 10% and prefix_cache_compat true. But we should run the eval harness on canary traffic before wide release.

ops-bot: [ALERT] regression-detection pinned: summarization drop 0.07 on `summarize-news-50` (compare baseline: 0.92 -> 0.85). Ticket created: INF-8741.

kai: INF-8741 has traces and sample requests. I added per-request kernel metadata to help trace which kernel was used.

sam: Ownership matrix for this thread: maria (quality lead / triage), ravi (quant profiles / code), lin (batching & cache), kai (metrics & instrumentation), sam (release decision).

maria: timeline proposal: today — flip to canary 10% + enable prefix_cache_compat. Tomorrow — run 6-hour canary eval and post results. If no further drop, widen to 50% next week. If regression persists, revert to previous profile.

ravi: I'll prep the rollback PR and the canary rollout change now. CC: @lin for cache toggle change.

lin: I'll coordinate infra quota check with eng-sre before canary (GPU slots for dual-profile canary). @sam can you nudge eng-sre if we need extra capacity?

sam: pinging eng-sre channel now.

maria: small code-review asks: @ravi please add an explicit test for long-context prompt fidelity in the eval harness and add a note to the release PR about observed cache/hash differences. Also tag this PR with `regression-watch` so the console can surface it.

ravi: on it. PR will include the new eval test and a short blurb. Expect it in ~90m.

maria: thanks. If anyone spots any additional failing prompt samples, drop them in the INF-8741 thread. I'll keep the rollout plan updated there and in this thread. :eyes:

sam: thanks all — appreciate the quick sync. :thumbsup:
